chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Taymuli, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from a man from our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When it is the days of the season (Hajj), Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends angels in the forms of humans who buy the provisions of the pilgrims and the merchants. I said, 'So what do they do with it?' He said, 'They throw it into the sea.'

key_terms.الْمَوْسِمِ: The season, specifically referring to the Hajj pilgrimage season

ai.seo_question: What do angels do with the goods bought from pilgrims during Hajj?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this unique tradition where angels, disguised as humans, purchase pilgrims' goods and cast them into the sea, symbolizing the divine acceptance and preservation of their offerings. This phenomenon highlights the spiritual economy of the Hajj season, where material transactions are transformed into acts of worship, reflecting the belief that Allah directly sustains the pilgrims during this sacred time.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Ibrahim Al Taymuly, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from a man from our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever it is the days for the season (of the Hajj), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sends Angels in images of the humans buying the provisions of the pilgrims and the merchants’. I said, ‘So what are they doing with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Throwing it into the sea’.
en.sarwar: 36. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Taymuliy from Ali ibn Asbat from a man from our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that during al-Hajj season Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, sends angels in the form of people to buy the goods of the pilgrims and merchants.”
I then asked, ‘What do they do with them?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘They throw them in the sea.’”
